content.value: Direction

LAND, RECONCILE, THEN MAKE THE NEGOTIATION VISIBLE. Three movements, four dispatch rounds, and the epic's own top-level acceptance criterion — a live 900px measurement on guerrilla — closed inside this wave rather than deferred to a wave that may never come.

Movement 1 — LAND (round 0). Get #4425, #4426, #4427 and #4428 onto main with the blocking gates green and the advisory Format red correctly ignored. Nothing else dispatches until all three round-1 seams are on main, because s4 imports the CSS bucket attribute + window.bpWidthBucket, the width_bucket assign + phx_hook attr, and display_state/4 in one breath.

content.value: The crush fix is the wave's floor, not its ceiling. If this wave ends with s4 merged and the desk structurally correct but visually unchanged, unanimated, keyboard-hostile at the strip, and unmeasured on the live host, it has not met the Kinsta/Vercel bar the epic set for itself. Prioritise in this order: land round 1, land s4, then s5-core + s6 (both halves), then the seal and the live proof. Every premium addition beyond s5's core is explicitly droppable in place — the PR must stay mergeable at the core.
Direction debate

RIVAL A — Pure roadmap execution. Dispatch exactly s4, then s5+s6 as written, then s7; add nothing. The argument is strong: the charter is ratified, the briefs already carry LAND-wave corrections verified against origin/main, the crush is already fixed by s1, and root.html.heex is guarded by a two-directional literal ratchet plus a generated byte-compare mirror check — every extra line in that file is a chance to red round 3 and strand round 4. Rejected because it ends the wave structurally right and experientially flat: the strip a11y defect ships AMPLIFIED (the wave makes that strip the primary back-nav at narrow), the desk animates nothing, the newly-undocked inspector gets no overlay treatment, and the epic's own live-measurement criterion goes unmet with no owner. But Rival A wins one point outright, and the winner absorbs it: s5's scope is ORDERED, its core lands as its own commit, and the premium additions are droppable without reopening the PR.

RIVAL B — Experience-first pivot. Defer s5's typography and font work entirely; spend round 3's single shell slot on motion, overlay affordance, focus and a live browser proof harness, on the theory that 'visibly reasons about space' is a motion claim, not a font claim. Rejected on two counts. First, D14's type-scale-and-Plex-Mono work is the unified-aesthetic debt this epic explicitly took on, it is already fully researched down to the copy-source paths, and no other epic owns it — deferring strands it. Second and decisively, typography and motion live in the SAME 5000-line style block, so deferring one buys no parallelism at all; it just leaves the round's single owner slot half-used. The winner absorbs Rival B's truth by merging it: round 3's shell owner does both, and the visible-reasoning work is promoted from nice-to-have to named acceptance criteria.

RIVAL C — Land-only wave. Given three PRs still open and UNSTABLE, spend the wave landing round 1 and s4 and stop. Rejected as timid: charter D20 already proved all three branches gate-green individually AND stacked, the wish explicitly asks for rounds 3 and 4 where verify proves file-disjointness, and a wave that consumes a full cycle to advance one round makes the remaining roadmap a three-wave tail.

WHY THE WINNER WON. It is the only candidate that both respects the binding constraint and refuses to be limited by it. The constraint is not effort or risk — it is that root.html.heex admits exactly one owner per round, which caps the wave at four serial rounds no matter how much money is spent. Given that cap, the correct move is not to shrink each round (Rival A) or to reshuffle what goes in it (Rival B) but to make each round's single shell slot carry the maximum coherent scope, and to push everything that is NOT the shell — semantics, tests, docs, live measurement — into the parallel lanes beside it.

The entire schedule is serialized on root.html.heex, and the winner hands its round-3 owner six concerns inside a 5000-line style block guarded by design/check.mjs Part E — an exemptions ratchet pinned at 165 that fails on GROWTH AND SHRINK and which lit-allow does not exempt — plus a generated paper-surface byte compare and a literal check. One miscount reds round 3; a red round 3 blocks round 4; the wave ends with the epic unsealed and the live proof unrun. HOW THE WAVE ABSORBS IT: (a) s5's scope is strictly ORDERED — core first as its own commit, premium additions as separate droppable commits, so the PR is mergeable at any prefix; (b) surveyors must prove BEFORE any builder flies exactly how the 165 count is computed, whether comment text and @font-face url() strings can move it, and what --write on the mirror check actually rewrites; (c) s7 is decoupled from s5 — its parity, measure-pin and doc work depends on s4, not s5, so a slipped round 3 still lets round 4 seal; (d) s9's live proof measures whatever actually merged and reports honestly, so it produces a real epic artefact even in the degraded case.

content.value: VERIFICATION RESULTS — what the deep round proved and refuted

Headline: Movement 1 of the strategic direction no longer exists. #4425 (c305c2096), #4426 (48402968f), #4427 (39ed4ab71) and #4428 (e73ea8c74) were ALL merged to origin/main between 18:12:03Z and 18:23:13Z, in charter order, with main's own `elixir` workflow green. LAND is a ledger stamp, not work — the wave starts at reconciliation and the four-round cap gained real slack.
REFUTED — five direction-level claims the evidence overturned

1. spd-s4's narrow rule closes ZERO pixels. A browser sweep over 384 configurations found overflow boundaries bit-identical under today's collapse?/3 and under display_state/4 — "today-n4: overflow for w in [640, 843]; clean from 844" and "s4-n4: overflow for w in [640, 843]; clean from 844". An independent Elixir matrix agreed: "narrow-vs-wide diffs with has_editor=TRUE: []". Cause: collapse?/3 already sets keep_full_nav_count = 1 when an editor is open, which IS idx == n-1. The CSS comment now on main at root.html.heex:1152-1161 promises an overflow removal this slice as briefed does not perform. -> D35 widens s4.

2. The real remaining crush is .bp-secondary-pane, and nobody had reached it. It is a DIRECT flex child of .pane-layout (components.ex:921-926 -> editor_fields.ex:84), flex: 0 0 360px at root.html.heex:2931-2932, with no responsive rule at any bucket — the phone rules touch only .pane-column and .editor-panel. Measured: "w=1024 n=1 ep=560 rowOver=80", "w=600 n=1 ep=240", "w=500 n=1 ep=140", "w=375 n=1 ep=15 text=0px rowOver=0". rowOver=0 means the D34 scroll valve never fires — the document is annihilated silently. -> D36 puts it in s4.

3. The 55ch floor floors the BORDER box, so the epic's own top criterion FAILS on merged code. box-sizing: border-box is global (:573) and .bp-paper-surface carries padding: 56px 40px (:3212-3217). Measured at a 900px viewport on the merged CSS: n=2 -> textPx 516, ch 51.5; n=3/4 -> 480px, 47.9ch. D31's recorded "596px = 67.6ch" implies ~8.82px/ch, which is Inter@14px (measured 8.75) — the CHROME font. That measurement never rendered the paper serif. Real advances at 18px, measured through the actual served woff2: Iowan 10.011px, self-hosted Source Serif 4 9.18px, Georgia 11.048px. -> D38.

4. The failure surface is .editor-body, not .editor-panel, and it is invisible on macOS. .editor-body declares only overflow-y: auto (:1563), so the spec promotes overflow-x to auto and IT becomes the scroll container: measured "eb_scrollW 608, eb_clientW 560, EB_SCROLLS true" under Georgia while "PANEL_scrollW 560, PANEL_clientW 560, PANEL_SCROLLS false" — and false under Iowan. A test aimed at .editor-panel passes vacuously forever. Bonus casualty: the 48ch .editor-body floor at :1230 is DEAD, beaten by .editor-with-preview .editor-panel-main { min-width: 0 } at :1624 (equal specificity, later source order); Chrome computes min-width "0px" in every configuration. -> D39, D40.

5. The media-modal regression does not exist, and D33's mechanism is empirically false. A browser A/B of the pre-s1 and post-s1 .editor-panel rules found the fixed modal byte-identical in both — "pre modal x0 w1440 h900" / "post containerType inline-size, modal x0 w1440 h900", backdrop still hit-testable 180px outside the panel, card still centred on the viewport (720) not the panel (840) — while two positive controls in the same run, contain: layout and transform: translateZ(0), BOTH promoted it (x240 w1200). Sweeping container-type across inline-size/size/normal left it at x0 in all three while an injected @container rule DID apply. Chrome deliberately does not treat container-type's layout containment as a containing block for fixed descendants. And media_live.ex has no folder affordance and no position:fixed at all — the "New folder modal" never existed. -> D41 keeps the carve-out as cross-engine insurance and re-scopes b10 to a tripwire.
PROVEN — what verification confirmed and made buildable

spd-s5's core is ratchet-neutral, executed step by step against the live gates: font copy + three @font-face blocks -> "root.html.heex 165 165 0 ok"; --font-mono repoint -> delta 0; ALL 175 exact-match font-size sites swapped -> delta 0; .text-xs drift fixed -> delta 0; final combined 199+/177- in one file with all four gates PASS and --write never needed. Both failure modes were demonstrated: "Part E FAIL: GREW 165 -> 166 (+1)" on a hand-written rgba(), "SHRANK 165 -> 164 (-1)" on a tokenised hex, and the house idiom hsl(var(--bp-shadow-hsl) / 0.2) returns it to 165. lit-allow appears 0 times in check.mjs.

The s4 seam is complete and inert on all three sides, and a probe diff built it end to end: Part E 165/165 delta 0, studio-literal-check PASS (367 files), studio-link-lint PASS, paper-editor-mirror PASS without --write, mix compile --warnings-as-errors exit 0, and "1867 tests, 0 failures" across the Studio surface. The hook round-trip was proven element-targeted on a NON-admin socket: "PROOF element-targeted pushEvent landed: width_bucket=\"phone\" admin=false".

The collapse morph animates for free. components.ex:576 derives the pane id purely from pane.title, so LiveView patches the node instead of replacing it; a width transition interpolated smoothly at a steady 60fps (31 consecutive rAF deltas 14.9-18.5ms, INP 55ms, CLS 0.0247) and simultaneous 3-pane toggles tracked an identical curve frame-for-frame. But the inner subtree swaps synchronously in the click tick — "immediateWidth 260.19, immediateHTML already collapsed" — so a bare width transition shows a tiny vertical label in a nearly-full-width box for ~150ms. -> D45.

The constraint is not effort or risk — it is that root.html.heex admits exactly one owner per round, which caps the wave at four serial rounds no matter how much money is spent. A browser sweep over 384 configurations found overflow boundaries bit-identical under today's collapse?/3 and under display_state/4 — "today-n4: overflow for w in [640, 843]; clean from 844" and "s4-n4: overflow for w in [640, 843]; clean from 844". 2. The real remaining crush is .bp-secondary-pane, and nobody had reached it. It is a DIRECT flex child of .pane-layout (components.ex:921-926 -> editor_fields.ex:84), flex: 0 0 360px at root.html.heex:2931-2932, with no responsive rule at any bucket — the phone rules touch only .pane-column and .editor-panel. Measured at a 900px viewport on the merged CSS: n=2 -> textPx 516, ch 51.5; n=3/4 -> 480px, 47.9ch. Real advances at 18px, measured through the actual served woff2: Iowan 10.011px, self-hosted Source Serif 4 9.18px, Georgia 11.048px. -> D38.

4. The failure surface is .editor-body, not .editor-panel, and it is invisible on macOS. .editor-body declares only overflow-y: auto (:1563), so the spec promotes overflow-x to auto and IT becomes the scroll container: measured "eb_scrollW 608, eb_clientW 560, EB_SCROLLS true" under Georgia while "PANEL_scrollW 560, PANEL_clientW 560, PANEL_SCROLLS false" — and false under Iowan. Chrome deliberately does not treat container-type's layout containment as a containing block for fixed descendants. Studio Space-Priority Desk — ADVANCE wave (2026-07-19)

Living wave paper for the ADVANCE wave (round 2+) of the studio-space-priority-desk epic (bp task studio-space-priority-desk). The design is RATIFIED (charter .claude/workflows/bp-studio-space-priority-desk-charter.md, D1-D32; the D19-D32 LAND amendments live in the merged rotating slot commit ec1fd170c). Round 1 was RESCUED by the LAND wave and is in flight as PRs #4425 (spd-s1 CSS foundation), #4426 (spd-s2 bucket server seam), #4427 (spd-s3 pane anatomy) plus #4428 (charter log) — all still OPEN at strategize time. This wave lands them and then advances rounds 2, 3 and 4 to the wave-1 roadmap's end. Every builder runs on OPUS (Fable 5 is spend-limited; a fable-assigned slice dies instantly — charter D19).

Wave status

REVIEW COMPLETE — wave closed 2026-07-19, grade A. Round 1 built four file-disjoint-in-intent slices (spd-s4, spd-b10, spd-bl, spd-b2); all four are gate-green on their review branches and ready for the lead to merge. Rounds 2-3 (spd-s5, spd-s6, spd-s7, then spd-s9) were NOT built this run by the sequenced-rounds law and dispatch as their dependencies merge. The debrief at the foot of this paper is the authoritative account; the STRATEGIZE-era text this block used to carry ('19 scouts dispatched next', 'we are BEFORE the survey digest') was superseded by the Digest, Verify and Decide sections below and has been replaced rather than left to mislead.

The wish

Verbatim constraints carried into this wave: (1) MODEL — every slice dispatches with builder_model 'opus', never 'fable', overriding the charter roadmap table. (2) LAND FIRST — verify #4425/#4426/#4427 on main; anything still open and red is job one, because round 2 imports all three seams. (3) ROUND 2 = spd-s4-bucket-reconciliation: register the WidthBucket hook in root.html.heex's Hooks block (navigate by the Hooks.EditorFocus marker, never a line number), pass phx_hook to <.pane_layout id="studio-panes">, consume display_state/4 in the pane loop, stamp data-role="content" on ALL FIVE .editor-panel roots (D29) with SCOPED selectors only (D30 — never the bare .bp-paper-surface, which is shared with the public reader, chat and swatch surfaces). (4) ROUND 3 where verify proves file-disjointness: spd-s5-desk-restyle and spd-s6-phone-drill. (5) ROUND 4: spd-s7 seals. (6) ROUNDS ARE LAW — no slice dispatches beside an unmerged dependency; root.html.heex is SINGLE-OWNER per round. (7) GATE ROSTER for every root.html.heex edit: scripts/studio-literal-check.sh AND design/check.mjs Part E (exemptions.json ratchet pinned at 165, fails on BOTH growth and shrink, lit-allow does NOT exempt it) AND scripts/paper-editor-mirror-check.sh (run with --write when the surface changes). web-literal-check.sh does NOT scope root.html.heex. .ex/.heex WAIT for the Elixir gate; check main's OWN gate before blaming a PR. (8) Stay on the Studio surface (barkpark_web layouts/studio/live) — concurrent cycles hold cloud/ (GUI remake) and api/tenancy + internal/cli (PDS), and a third holds tasks/design (TLV). (9) File as many well-decomposed opus slices as the verified survey supports.

Ground truth at strategize

• PRs #4425 (root.html.heex only, +203/-8), #4426 (6 files, server seam + tests), #4427 (pane_builder.ex + test, +264) and #4428 (charter log) are ALL OPEN, mergeStateStatus UNSTABLE, with blocking checks still IN_PROGRESS and the Format job FAILING — which charter D23 declares advisory-by-design and RED on main itself.
• The bp ledger shows spd-s1/s2/s3 in_progress (7/8, 4/6, 5/6 criteria met) — the unmet ones are the 'merged to main' criteria the lead closes on merge, exactly as designed.
• spd-s4..s7 are open with 0 criteria met. Fifteen backlog children exist: b1 pane-state persistence, b2 docs-anchors prune, b3 dead admin-shell CSS, b4 stamp-2532, b5 navshell triage, b6 sub-500px proof, b7 protected-measure clamp, b8 .editor-panel blast radius, b9 merge-gates doc currency, b10 container/fixed-position audit, bl api-tester flex retire.
• s1's landed CSS is high quality and honest: a documented overflow-x escape valve on .pane-layout, flat 55ch/48ch floors scoped to .editor-panel, a 560px content floor, container-name:content with position:relative, an explicit containment carve-out for .editor-panel.sheet-editor (position:fixed descendants), and the FULL .bp-desk-crumbs CSS pre-provisioned for s6.
• s3's display_state/4 keeps collapse?/3 verbatim as the wide/standard reducer; collapse?/3 keeps 1 full nav pane when an editor is open and 2 otherwise.
• The collapsed pane strip is a plain <div> with phx-click (panes.ex:87) — no role, no tabindex, no keyboard path, no aria-expanded. At the narrow bucket this wave PROMOTES that strip to the desk's primary back-navigation.
• docs/cards/studio.md says nothing about the anatomy model, buckets or the protected measure — its Layout section still reads as a pre-wave document.

Direction

LAND, RECONCILE, THEN MAKE THE NEGOTIATION VISIBLE. Three movements, four dispatch rounds, and the epic's own top-level acceptance criterion — a live 900px measurement on guerrilla — closed inside this wave rather than deferred to a wave that may never come.

Movement 1 — LAND (round 0). Get #4425, #4426, #4427 and #4428 onto main with the blocking gates green and the advisory Format red correctly ignored. Nothing else dispatches until all three round-1 seams are on main, because s4 imports the CSS bucket attribute + window.bpWidthBucket, the width_bucket assign + phx_hook attr, and display_state/4 in one breath.

Movement 2 — RECONCILE (round 2). spd-s4 is the wave's spine and the sole owner of root.html.heex and studio_live/components.ex this round: hook live, display_state/4 consumed, data-role stamped on all five .editor-panel roots plus the pane columns and the inspector, interim narrow CSS retired where the server now renders strips. Beside it, only work that is provably file-disjoint fans out — measurement, docs and the api_tester residue — never a second editor of the shell.

Movement 3 — MAKE IT VISIBLE (rounds 3 and 4). This is where the wave stops being merely correct. The epic's vision sentence is 'a layout system that VISIBLY REASONS about space' — and reasoning that is invisible is indistinguishable from a bug. So round 3's single root.html.heex owner (spd-s5) is deliberately WIDENED from a font-and-type-scale chore into the desk's premium pass, and round 3's .ex owner (spd-s6) is widened from a breadcrumb into THE WAY BACK.

• spd-s5 (root.html.heex, sole owner, ORDERED scope): CORE FIRST — self-hosted IBM Plex Mono copied from cloud/priv/static/fonts, --font-mono repointed, desk-chrome font sizes consuming var(--text-*) with the .text-xs 11-vs-12px drift resolved, .bp-secondary-pane yielding instead of holding a rigid 360px, .sheet-toolbar scrolling instead of clipping. THEN, as separately-droppable commits: motion on the collapse/expand negotiation with a prefers-reduced-motion opt-out; a real inspector-overlay treatment (scrim, elevation, a dismiss affordance) now that it stops being docked; focus-visible rings for every affordance this wave promotes; and the b3 dead admin-shell block plus the b7 upper measure clamp if the ratchet allows.
• spd-s6 (panes.ex + studio_live/components.ex, sole owner): the phone breadcrumb rendered as a SIBLING before <.pane_layout> per D27, AND the collapsed strip made keyboard-operable and screen-reader-honest (button semantics, aria-label, focus ring, a chevron that points the way it navigates). Crumbs and strips are the same story — the way back — and they are the same file owner. One coherent slice, not two colliding ones.
• spd-s7 (round 4, docs + tests only): the seal — view-edit parity matrix, the measure-parity assertion that pins the Studio protected measure against the public reader column with a loud selector-missing guard, the .editor-panel blast-radius acknowledgement, docs/cards/studio.md brought current, and the merge-gates doc corrected (there is no workflow named 'Elixir Test').
• spd-s9 NEW (round 4, evidence only): the LIVE PROOF. Measure the real Studio on guerrilla after deploy at 1440 / 1280 / 1024 / 900 / 640 / 500 px and record a measurement matrix — content-pane px and ch, whether the row scrolls horizontally, which panes are strips, whether the inspector overlays, whether the crumbs appear. This closes the epic's own criterion 'the default open-paper state at a 900px viewport holds >=55ch on guerrilla (live measurement, not inference)', which NO slice in the roadmap currently owns. It writes only evidence, so it collides with nothing.
What matters most
The crush fix is the wave's floor, not its ceiling. If this wave ends with s4 merged and the desk structurally correct but visually unchanged, unanimated, keyboard-hostile at the strip, and unmeasured on the live host, it has not met the Kinsta/Vercel bar the epic set for itself. Prioritise in this order: land round 1, land s4, then s5-core + s6 (both halves), then the seal and the live proof. Every premium addition beyond s5's core is explicitly droppable in place — the PR must stay mergeable at the core.

Direction debate

RIVAL A — Pure roadmap execution. Dispatch exactly s4, then s5+s6 as written, then s7; add nothing. The argument is strong: the charter is ratified, the briefs already carry LAND-wave corrections verified against origin/main, the crush is already fixed by s1, and root.html.heex is guarded by a two-directional literal ratchet plus a generated byte-compare mirror check — every extra line in that file is a chance to red round 3 and strand round 4. Rejected because it ends the wave structurally right and experientially flat: the strip a11y defect ships AMPLIFIED (the wave makes that strip the primary back-nav at narrow), the desk animates nothing, the newly-undocked inspector gets no overlay treatment, and the epic's own live-measurement criterion goes unmet with no owner. But Rival A wins one point outright, and the winner absorbs it: s5's scope is ORDERED, its core lands as its own commit, and the premium additions are droppable without reopening the PR.

RIVAL B — Experience-first pivot. Defer s5's typography and font work entirely; spend round 3's single shell slot on motion, overlay affordance, focus and a live browser proof harness, on the theory that 'visibly reasons about space' is a motion claim, not a font claim. Rejected on two counts. First, D14's type-scale-and-Plex-Mono work is the unified-aesthetic debt this epic explicitly took on, it is already fully researched down to the copy-source paths, and no other epic owns it — deferring strands it. Second and decisively, typography and motion live in the SAME 5000-line style block, so deferring one buys no parallelism at all; it just leaves the round's single owner slot half-used. The winner absorbs Rival B's truth by merging it: round 3's shell owner does both, and the visible-reasoning work is promoted from nice-to-have to named acceptance criteria.

RIVAL C — Land-only wave. Given three PRs still open and UNSTABLE, spend the wave landing round 1 and s4 and stop. Rejected as timid: charter D20 already proved all three branches gate-green individually AND stacked, the wish explicitly asks for rounds 3 and 4 where verify proves file-disjointness, and a wave that consumes a full cycle to advance one round makes the remaining roadmap a three-wave tail.

WHY THE WINNER WON. It is the only candidate that both respects the binding constraint and refuses to be limited by it. The constraint is not effort or risk — it is that root.html.heex admits exactly one owner per round, which caps the wave at four serial rounds no matter how much money is spent. Given that cap, the correct move is not to shrink each round (Rival A) or to reshuffle what goes in it (Rival B) but to make each round's single shell slot carry the maximum coherent scope, and to push everything that is NOT the shell — semantics, tests, docs, live measurement — into the parallel lanes beside it.

The sharpest attack on the winner
The entire schedule is serialized on root.html.heex, and the winner hands its round-3 owner six concerns inside a 5000-line style block guarded by design/check.mjs Part E — an exemptions ratchet pinned at 165 that fails on GROWTH AND SHRINK and which lit-allow does not exempt — plus a generated paper-surface byte compare and a literal check. One miscount reds round 3; a red round 3 blocks round 4; the wave ends with the epic unsealed and the live proof unrun. HOW THE WAVE ABSORBS IT: (a) s5's scope is strictly ORDERED — core first as its own commit, premium additions as separate droppable commits, so the PR is mergeable at any prefix; (b) surveyors must prove BEFORE any builder flies exactly how the 165 count is computed, whether comment text and @font-face url() strings can move it, and what --write on the mirror check actually rewrites; (c) s7 is decoupled from s5 — its parity, measure-pin and doc work depends on s4, not s5, so a slipped round 3 still lets round 4 seal; (d) s9's live proof measures whatever actually merged and reports honestly, so it produces a real epic artefact even in the degraded case.

SECOND LOAD-BEARING ASSUMPTION. The winner assumes #4425/#4426/#4427 merge cleanly on their blocking gates. If any is genuinely red on a BLOCKING check — not the advisory Format job, and not a main that is itself red — round 2 cannot start and movement 1 becomes the wave's real work. That is survey question one, and it is answered before anything else dispatches.

But the inner subtree swaps synchronously in the click tick — "immediateWidth 260.19, immediateHTML already collapsed" — so a bare width transition shows a tiny vertical label in a nearly-full-width box for ~150ms. -> D45.

The strip button conversion is free of test breakage: div -> <button type="button"> with aria-expanded, aria-label, mirrored chevron and aria-hidden svg passed all 26 pane tests, 51 pane/builder tests and the scope-guard test UNCHANGED. But it needs a UA reset that .pane-column--collapsed does not provide, and that CSS lives in root.html.heex. -> D46 splits it across s5 and s6 along the D28 file line.

The phone crumb needs zero new server events, proven through the call chain rather than assumed: expand_pane/2 (scope.ex:161-172) does Enum.take(nav_path, idx) and push_patches; handle_params -> Lifecycle.finish_handle_params -> Shared.rebuild_panes unconditionally re-assigns editor_doc from a fresh PaneBuilder.build/3, which seeds its walk with editor = nil (pane_builder.ex:71). editor_doc is DERIVED, never sticky, so crumb idx=0 provably closes the editor.

spd-s9 is mechanically runnable but was NOT runnable usefully. The D24e login-ticket flow worked end to end twice (201 ticket -> 302 + set-cookie -> /studio 200) and the px/ch recipe measured cleanly. But guerrilla was serving PRE-s1 code: build v0.2.25.1292, window.bpWidthBucket undefined, the old ".pane-layout { display: flex; flex: 1; overflow: hidden; }", and a 900px measurement of "290px / 29ch" — the un-fixed crush. Root cause: push-triggered CI had gone silent repo-wide (check-runs total_count: 0 on every main commit including HEAD). -> D47 makes a deploy proof s9's first criterion.

COVERAGE — including the not-founds

Four separate verifiers reported not_found for the charter path their brief named: .claude/workflows/bp-studio-space-priority-charter.md and .claude/workflows/bp-studio-space-priority-desk-charter.md both failed against origin/main, where the epic's D1-D34 lived in the rotating slot .claude/workflows/bp-cloud-epic-charter.md. D37 settles it and the wave's Decide phase wrote the durable file. Also not found: any test that would fail if the wide bucket stopped being byte-identical (D7 is prose plus a manual measurement); any test pinning s3's role:/priority: values; any a11y gate anywhere in CI (design/check.mjs Part H is colour-contrast only, and no axe/pa11y/eslint-jsx-a11y runs); any --text-* rung below 12px while 94 desk sites sit under it; any committed measurement harness (D24e is a procedure, not a script); any deploy-latency figure in-repo. One verifier also found `bp task ls --limit/--offset` silently ignores offset and `bp task ls --all` hard-errors with pagination_stalled — `bp doc ls task` was the working path (2056 task documents, zero duplicate ids).

Two corrections to prior digests, recorded so they do not propagate: the paper-editor-mirror SHELL script DOES scope root.html.heex (6 references, HEEX= at :53) even though the .mjs does not (0) — --write is genuinely unneeded for this wave's diffs, but the scope claim was wrong. And there are SIX .editor-panel roots, not the five D29 enumerates: sheet_grid.ex:2478 is the sixth (D42).

DECISIONS — D35 through D47

Each mirrors the charter at .claude/workflows/bp-studio-space-priority-charter.md; the charter is the epic's memory, this Paper is the wave's story.

WAVE PLAN — 8 slices, 3 dispatch rounds, every builder on opus (D19)

ROUNDS ARE LAW. Round 1 dispatches now. A round-2 slice does NOT build this run — the lead dispatches it after its dependency MERGES. root.html.heex has exactly one owner per round (D16): spd-s4 in round 1, spd-s5 in round 2. Every brief is deliberately SELF-CONTAINED, because the durable charter is committed but not yet on origin/main (filed as spd-b14).

Backlog filed this wave as published children: spd-b11-subxs-type-scale (the type scale has no rung below 12px while 94 desk sites sit under it), spd-b12-inspector-overlay-dismiss (the overlay CSS shipped in s1; the scrim, Escape, aria-modal and focus management did not), spd-b13-foreign-file-claim-fence (two ready, unclaimed non-SPD tasks declare root.html.heex and studio_live/components.ex in their files arrays), spd-b14-charter-path-durability (the durable charter is committed to local main and therefore still invisible to worktree builders). Folded rather than filed: spd-b8 and spd-b9 into spd-s7; spd-b3 and spd-b7 into spd-s5's droppable tier; spd-b6 into spd-s9's matrix.

DEBRIEF — Review (2026-07-19)

One reviewer, four green slices, every gate re-run on the final branches. Two cross-slice defects were found and FIXED in place; nothing was handed back to a builder. The wave's own file-disjointness claim turned out to be false in two places, which is the single most important lesson to carry forward.

What shipped, per slice

The two cross-slice defects — and why they matter more than either bug

Both defects are the same failure mode: a slice declared itself file-disjoint on the strength of what it EDITS, while its coupling to a sibling ran through what it READS or through a neighbouring line. spd-s4's bp `files` label omitted panes.ex even though the slice edits it, so the dispatch frontier's collision check could not see the spd-bl overlap; that label has been corrected in the ledger. spd-b10 edits nothing but its own test file and is genuinely disjoint by the frontier's rules, yet it hard-coded line numbers in a file spd-s4 rewrites — disjoint by ownership, coupled by content.

The rule this wave earned Never pin a source location by line number in a guard. Pin it by an anchor that only moves when the thing itself is rewritten. A line-number pin turns every unrelated neighbour edit into a false red, which trains readers to ignore the tripwire — the exact opposite of what a tripwire is for.

What the lead must know before merging

  • MERGE ORDER: spd-s4-…-0-r first, then spd-bl-…-2-r (which is stacked on it), then spd-b10-…-1-r and spd-b2-…-3-r in any order. Merging spd-bl before spd-s4 is not possible; merging spd-b10's ORIGINAL branch (not the -r) alongside spd-s4 reds main.
  • MERGE-GATED CRITERIA the lead closes on merge: spd-s4 criterion 8, spd-b10 criterion 5, spd-bl criterion 4, spd-b2 criterion 3 — all worded 'PR merged to main after the elixir workflow's Test (Elixir 1.18.1 / OTP 27.0) job is green'. Every other criterion is already stamped with evidence.
  • A11Y REGRESSION WINDOW, opened deliberately by spd-s4 and closed only by spd-s5 + spd-s6 together: at narrow with a document open, the ONLY navigation affordance is now a plain <div phx-click> with no role, tabindex, aria-expanded or focus ring, wearing a chevron-RIGHT glyph on an action that goes BACK. Keyboard users on a narrow desk have no back-nav until BOTH round-2 slices land. This argues for dispatching s5 and s6 together and merging them close in time.
  • NOT PROVEN BY ANY GATE: every CSS claim in spd-s4. mix test renders no layout and design/check.mjs audits only tokens and literals. The D40 specificity arithmetic, the 720px container gate and the .bp-secondary-pane yield are all reasoned, not measured. spd-s9 is where they get measured; do not treat green CI as a rendering proof.
  • ONE UNIDENTIFIED FLAKE: the Studio-surface suite failed once in six consecutive review runs on the same tree and could not be reproduced (5/6 green, 1884 tests). The failure text was not captured. Treat a single red on these directories as suspect before blaming a PR — and check main's own elixir gate first.

Ledger audit

HONEST. All four slice tasks sit in_progress with per-criterion evidence stamped as the work happened, merge criteria correctly left open for the lead, and every one linked to this paper via wave_paper. The four deferred slices (spd-s5, spd-s6, spd-s7, spd-s9) are open, unclaimed and untouched since Decide. Two builders filed their own discovered gaps as published children rather than quietly fixing or dropping them — task-2d359bf4fbe44929 (the secondary pane is CSS-hidden but still server-rendered and still open server-side) and spd-b10f-fixed-census-paper-editor-css. One ledger correction was made: spd-s4's `files` array gained panes.ex. One new child was filed from this review: spd-b14-measure-floor-font-audit — calc(55ch + 80px) is sized from two measured faces (Iowan ~631px, Georgia ~688px) and a face above ~11.6px/ch would push the floor past the 720px container gate and re-materialise the D39 horizontal scroll in a thin band.

Grade — A

Earned, not given. What is genuinely strong: the wave did the hard thing the charter demanded rather than the briefed thing. D35 was a measured no-op and spd-s4 replaced it with a rule that actually closes the 640-1023 band; D36 found and killed the last unconditional crush; D38/D40 corrected a floor that had never once applied on the paper path and re-landed a dead rule at specificity that outranks its competitor. spd-b10's tripwires were both demonstrated to fire, and spd-b2 proved its performance fix result-set-identical in two independent experiments instead of just quoting a stopwatch. Builder self-reviews were unusually honest — every one named what it could not prove, and two filed their gaps as tasks. What falls short: round 1's file-disjointness was asserted rather than verified, and it was false twice, which is exactly the class of error the rounds law exists to prevent; a reviewer should not be the first person to run two round-1 branches together. spd-s4 also knowingly opens an accessibility hole it does not close. Neither is a correctness defect in what ships, and both were fixed or documented here — hence A, not A+ and not A-.

Next wave — dispatch order

  • MERGE round 1 in order: spd-s4 (-r), then spd-bl (-r, stacked), then spd-b10 (-r) and spd-b2 (-r). Close the four merge-gated criteria.
  • THEN ROUND 2, all three after spd-s4 merges: spd-s5-desk-restyle (sole owner of root.html.heex; ordered core-then-droppable per D43) and spd-s7-parity-guard-card (docs + measure assertion, decoupled from s5) dispatch together; spd-s6-phone-drill-breadcrumb needs spd-bl merged too, since it claims panes.ex. Dispatch s5 and s6 in the SAME round and merge them close together — the a11y hole spd-s4 opened needs both halves (s5's UA reset + focus ring in root.html.heex, s6's <button> markup in panes.ex).
  • THEN ROUND 3: spd-s9-live-measure-proof, gated on the D47 deploy PROOF (ssh git log -1 on /opt/barkpark, cross-checked against barkpark-slot@blue.service) before a single measurement is taken.
  • Carry spd-b14-measure-floor-font-audit into whichever wave owns the live browser session — it is cheap to fold into spd-s9's matrix.
  • Charter housekeeping for the next Decide: D42's six-root census is now stated in LINE NUMBERS that spd-s4 has already invalidated (components.ex 797/861 are now ~809/874). The guard no longer depends on them, but a brief that quotes them will send a builder to the wrong place. Quote the anchors instead.
